metadataReview.note: The scholarly literature names the March 1591 defeat of Askia Ishaq II’s Songhay army by Judar Pasha’s Moroccan force after Tondibi, on the Niger bend north of Gao. The atlas point marks Tondibi hamlet as a village-sector reference; the Wikipedia summary, citing Gomez (2018), places the meeting at Tankondibogho near Tondibi, which no gazetteer consulted locates. The existing date (12 March 1591) is retained; the 13 March given by the Wikipedia summary is not adopted. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: OpenStreetMap node 2162066832 (place=hamlet, name Tondibi, Cercle de Gao, Mali; tagged with NGA GNS feature UFI -1076277) is at latitude 16.6563239, longitude -0.2202997, rounded to [-0.2203,16.6563]. It is the only Tondibi settlement the gazetteer returns in Mali and lies on the Niger north of Gao, consistent with Reid’s “northeast bend of the Niger” and the Wikipedia summary “near Tondibi, just north of Gao”. This is an eponymous village reference, not the exact field at Tankondibogho (not located), the Songhay or Moroccan lines, or a surveyed centre. No accuracy radius is claimed.
